transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I've barely been sleeping lately. Not since this warehouse inspection I had to do for work. I just kind of lie there at night, replaying bits of what happened. And even when I do manage to drift off, I wake up a little while later, completely sweaty and wide awake. It's like... like I'm right back near that blast again.
Have you been avoiding anything that reminds you of the warehouse inspection?

Yes, actually. I've been completely avoiding the file for that specific warehouse. I just... I can't look at it. And honestly, I've been letting any calls about industrial accounts go straight to voicemail. Even just opening emails related to those kinds of properties makes my stomach drop, so I just avoid them altogether.
Have you experienced any moments where you felt like you were reliving the warehouse inspection?

Yes, I have. Um, sometimes during the day, I’ll just be at work reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report, and... I suddenly get hit with this really sharp image of the worker on the floor, and all the soot in the air. It just happens out of nowhere, and it feels like my body physically reacts to it before I can even stop it.
Are there any people, places, or activities you've been avoiding because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?

Um, not really, no. Not any specific people or places, anyway. Like I said a minute ago, it's really just those work activities—the files and the calls about industrial properties. But outside of that... no, I haven't noticed myself avoiding going anywhere else or seeing anyone in particular. Just those specific work tasks.
Have you been having difficulty concentrating?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any issues with my focus or concentration, at least not more than usual. When I'm working on other types of accounts, I seem to be able to get through them just fine. It's really just the industrial ones that are the problem.
Do you find yourself being constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats?

No, I wouldn't say so. Um, I haven't really noticed myself doing that. I don't feel like I'm constantly looking over my shoulder or watching out for threats in my day-to-day life or anything. I'm just going about things normally, for the most part.
Have you been startled more easily than usual since the warehouse inspection?

Yes, actually, I have. It's been really noticeable at the office. Every time a printer jams, or a door slams, or even if someone just walks up behind my desk, I jump like something terrible is happening. My heart just starts racing, and it takes me several minutes to finally settle down and feel normal again. It's really frustrating.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened during the warehouse inspection?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I was just there to do my job for the underwriting assessment. I don't feel like it was my fault or that I could have done anything differently to prevent it. So, no, I really don't feel responsible for it.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since the warehouse inspection?
It's been going on for about a week now. Basically, ever since the warehouse inspection... when the explosion happened.
Have you avoided talking to anyone about what happened during the warehouse inspection?

Yes, I have. I really don't want to discuss it with anyone. But it's not just talking... I've actually been avoiding the warehouse file at work, too. I've been letting any calls about our industrial accounts just go straight to voicemail. Honestly, even just opening those emails makes my stomach drop. So, yeah, I'm just trying to avoid all of it.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I normally do outside of work. I'll still watch my favorite shows or go for a run... it's mostly just the work stuff and anything related to the warehouse that I'm struggling with. So, no, my interest in my regular hobbies is pretty much the same.
Have you avoided talking to friends or family about the warehouse inspection because of the memories or feelings it brings up?

Yeah, like I mentioned a minute ago, I really just don't want to discuss it with anyone. That includes my friends and family. They know I was there, but... I just tell them I don't want to talk about it. It's just easier to not bring it up at all, so I don't have to think about it.
Have you noticed any decrease in interest in activities that you previously enjoyed, outside of work?

No, um, like I mentioned a couple of minutes ago, I haven't really noticed any change there. I still enjoy my normal hobbies outside of work, like going for a run or watching my shows. It's really just the work stuff that's the problem.
Have you felt less interested in things you normally care about since the warehouse inspection?

Um, I think you just asked me that, but no. Like I was saying, my interest in the things I normally care about hasn't really changed. I'm still doing my usual hobbies and everything... it really is just the work stuff that's an issue right now.
Have you avoided social activities because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?
No, not really. I mean, social things don't really remind me of the inspection. Like I said, it's mostly just work-related stuff that I'm trying to avoid. I still see my friends and everything.
Have you felt less interested in things you normally care about since the warehouse inspection, outside of your work?

I feel like we're going in circles a bit here... but no, my answer is still the same. I haven't lost interest in anything outside of my job. I still care about my normal hobbies and everything else just as much as I did before the inspection.
Have you ever felt like you were outside of your body, watching yourself, since the warehouse inspection?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've always felt like myself, in my own body. I just... I get anxious and have trouble sleeping, but I've never felt like I was watching myself from the outside.
